criterion_notes.c1: Target record mismatch: metadata specifies Syaukat (2000), 'Economics of integrated surface and ground water use management in the Jakarta region, Indonesia', whereas the retrieved PDF is a different publication—Syaukat and Fox (2004), 'Conjunctive Surface and Ground Water Management in the Jakarta Region, Indonesia', JAWRA 40(1):241-250—which cites Syaukat (2000, unpublished Ph.D. thesis, University of Guelph, Canada) as a separate document. In the retrieved 2004 JAWRA paper, urban piped water supply (PAM Jaya) and ground water consumption across households, commercial/services, and industrial users are modelled at an aggregate regional level, while explicitly excluding distributional aspects of access to water; whether the unretrieved 2000 thesis/report also examined household water service access directly cannot be verified.
criterion_notes.c2: Target record mismatch leaves the 2000 thesis/report unclear. Evaluated on the retrieved 2004 JAWRA text alone: under the PLAIN wording of Criterion 2, it would pass (plain=yes) because it examines the economic inefficiency of institutional arrangements for surface and ground water management (de facto open access and unenforced deep-well quotas) and models aggregate vs. commercial/industrial ground water pumping quotas alongside PAM Jaya capital investment options (though the 2004 paper would still fail Criterion 3 for lack of empirical evidence, so plain_criterion2_decision on the 2004 paper alone would still be exclude). Under the NARROW 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2, the 2004 paper fails (narrow=no) because its modelled policy scenarios concern regional aquifer extraction caps (particularly commercial/industrial pumping quotas) and generic utility capital stock investment rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community water service access (such as connection eligibility, tenure/documentation rules, household tariff/cost-recovery rules, or disconnection/enforcement governing household access), with institutional permitting described only as unanalysed background. Because the 2000 target text itself was not retrieved, overall plain_criterion2_decision is cannot_tell.
criterion_notes.c3: Unclear for the unretrieved 2000 Ph.D. thesis/EEPSEA report (which the 2004 acknowledgments note was supported by an EEPSEA Doctoral Fieldwork Research Award and may contain primary fieldwork/survey data not reported here). The retrieved 2004 JAWRA paper itself contains no primary empirical analysis or observed policy evaluation; it constructs a calibrated dynamic nonlinear mathematical programming optimization model in GAMS/MINOS simulating counterfactual trajectories from 1999 to 2025 using secondary parameters, which on its own would be excluded for lacking empirical access evidence (E05/E12).

evidence_quotes.quote: Syaukat, Yusman and Glenn C. Fox, 2004. Conjunctive Surface and Ground Water Management in the Jakarta Region, Indonesia. Journal of the American Water Resources Association (JAWRA) 40(1):241-250.
For a more detailed exposition of the structure of the model, please see Y. Syaukat (2000, unpublished Ph.D. thesis, University of Guelph, Canada).

A numerical model of integrated surface and ground water management is developed using GAMS (General Algebraic Modelling System) software. The model maximizes the net present value of social benefits from piped water and ground water consumption across all users over time from 1999 to 2025.

The partial ground water pumping quota scenario limits total ground water extraction for commercial and industrial users to 40 percent of the recharge rate. These categories of users currently consume 47 percent of the ground water being extracted.
Note that this optimum does not reflect distributional aspects of access to water, nor does it reflect water quality issues or land subsidence costs.
Professor Syaukat acknowledges the Doctoral Fieldwork Research Award from the Economy and Environment Program for Southeast Asia (EEPSEA), Singapore.
